issue: Grammar sound. English 'My body is strong' stands over aorist Hwérdʰt 'has grown strong' (stretched); wos 'your (pl.)' words beside a 2sg addressee.
tóy séh₂etes: tóy is masc. NOM.PL (or neut. du.) while séh₂etes is a 2/3du subjunctive; subject and verb disagree in number. For the king and queen use tóh₁ séh₂etes; for the guests tóy séh₂onti.
dayh₂wḗr mluHénti: 3pl verb with a singular subject ('the husband's brother sings'); every parallel clause has 3sg mléwHti. Should be mléwHti. (mlewH- 'say' for 'sing' is a stretched sense.)
Grammar sound; h₁yód as 'if' and kʷéḱt poh₂imḗn tā́m déh₂newi match their English (the shepherd line is an odd non-sequitur but faithful).
Tier 1: Schleicher 1868 notation (no laryngeals, a-vocalism, akwams, bʰarantam); faithful to the source and matches the English.

sérpet-kʷe h₁éy próti: h₁éy is NOMINATIVE of the anaphor after próti 'toward them'; needs an accusative (closed class has no dual of *i-, so at least ACC.PL h₁íns). Also tóybʰos and usméy are plural for the two brothers (no dual dat. in closed class: engine gap, minor).
Grammar sound. mē + present dʰrugʰyéte for a prohibition (imperative-like; injunctive expected but accepted); English 'Hail, father-in-law! Hail, son-in-law!' adds 'Hail' over bare vocatives.
Grammar sound. English 'crept toward us' – próti has no object in the PIE.
